papers.title: Promoting fairness in LLMs: detection and mitigation of gender bias (Knowledge and Information Systems, 2026; DOI 10.1007/s10115-026-02731-3; no arXiv preprint - Research Square preprint rs-6461545; code at github.com/tejanshsachdeva/Biasness-Mitigation)

coauthors.name: Mitaali Singhal
coauthors.affiliation: Oracle (per LinkedIn snippet); co-author on the Shiv Nadar University fairness project
coauthors.relevance_evidence: Only indexed work is the shared paper 'Promoting fairness in LLMs: detection and mitigation of gender bias' (Semantic Scholar author 2425535609, paperCount=1). That work is gender/sensitive-attribute bias detection and LoRA-based mitigation measured with Disparity Index, Idea Consistency Score and Thematic Consistency Score over English and Hindi prompts. It is generic fairness/bias plus bilingual evaluation with no treatment of cultural values, cross-cultural value differences or value alignment, so it fails the cultural-values gate.

coauthors.name: Sonia Khetarpaul
coauthors.affiliation: Associate Professor, Department of Computer Science and Engineering, Shiv Nadar University, Dadri, India
coauthors.relevance_evidence: Senior author on the shared paper and, separately, author of 'Investigating Cultural Bias: A Comparative Study of Large Language Models' (PReMI 2025, DOI 10.1007/978-3-032-18477-1_45, Semantic Scholar paper b84aa574f14a31324446070993779e95a0b29a18, DBLP conf/premi/SrivastavaSKS25) - a comparative study of cultural bias across large language models, i.e. cultural bias in LLMs directly, not generic fairness. She also works on cross-lingual LLM QA ('CLOR-QA: Cross-Lingual Open-Retrieval Question Answering Model with Dynamic Database Integration', DOI 10.1007/978-3-031-78090-5_2) and Indian-context LLM adaptation ('IndLaw-QA: Fine-Tuned LLMs with RAG for Indian Legal QA'), but the cultural-bias LLM study alone satisfies the gate.
